title: 7th Sitting of first Session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened with the Minority Leader's reply to the President's address, which criticised the government's handling of the economy, housing, health, fisheries and other areas, with the Speaker repeatedly asking members to keep order. After a recess the House debated the Finance Committee report on the President's two-year cost-cutting plan, with several points of order and a dispute over whether remarks about the judiciary were on topic, and passed it 44-0. It then approved four non-resident ambassador appointments from the Foreign Relations Committee, sent two more nominations to that committee, and held the first reading of a bill amending the Courts Act. The attendance figures in item 2 and some of the opening text are partly garbled. This part of the minutes contains only the electronic voting records, with no speeches. Members voted in open votes on three nominations of non-resident ambassadors: to Luxembourg and the Netherlands, to France, and to Australia. Each nomination received only Yes votes, with no No votes or abstentions. Every vote had 74 members present and 73 eligible to vote, and 25 to 28 members did not cast a vote.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Said the President's address offered no plan for economic hardship, citing rising prices, a dollar shortage and unpaid government bills.
Argued the 2024 deficit, borrowing and negative usable reserves contradict campaign promises and the claim of a strong economy.
Criticised the China trade deal, housing, health and fisheries record, and raised concerns about media freedom, corruption and independent institutions.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Argued judicial pay cuts, alongside a bill to cut Supreme Court judges from seven to five, amount to government pressure on the court.
Objected to the chair interrupting him, saying this departs from past practice in the Majlis.
After the recess, repeated that the pay cuts and the bill to reduce Supreme Court seats threaten judicial independence.

speakers.name: Qasim Ibrahim
positions: Presented the Finance Committee report: some measures need law changes first, while salary reductions under the guidelines could save about 14 million rufiyaa a year.
Raised points of order saying the South Galolhu member was off topic and asked whether repeated interruptions should be limited.
Thanked the President for the cost-cutting plan and argued the deficit and unpaid bills require cuts, including subsidies.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Raised a point of order saying the debate had drifted from the report and cast aspersions on the President.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Raised a point of order that the South Galolhu member stayed off topic despite repeated chair warnings and alleged repeated untruths.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Said a strong economy matters for a state, backed expanding industries such as fisheries and supporting youth entrepreneurship.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Presented the Foreign Relations Committee report on four ambassador nominations, noting the committee agreed unanimously and no extra salary cost arises.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 1 to 3 accepted as passed.
Finance Committee report on the President's cost-cutting measures passed 44-0.
Dr. Mariyam Shabeena Ahmed (Malaysia-based) approved as non-resident ambassador to Brunei, 47-0.
Belgium-based ambassador approved as non-resident ambassador to Luxembourg and the Netherlands, 48-0.
UK-based ambassador approved as non-resident ambassador to France, 45-0.
Singapore-based ambassador approved as non-resident ambassador to Australia, 48-0.
Nominations for non-resident ambassadors to Russia and Morocco referred to the Foreign Relations Committee.
First reading held on the bill amending the Courts Act; next sitting set for Tuesday 25 Feb 2025 at 9:00.
Geela Ali's nomination as non-resident ambassador to Luxembourg and the Netherlands received 48 Yes votes and none against.
Iruthisham Adam's nomination as non-resident ambassador to France received 45 Yes votes and none against.
Mohamed Luveiz's nomination as non-resident ambassador to Australia received 48 Yes votes and none against.
